newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam to halve workforce, record charge.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam to halve workforce, record charge.

text.p: Appliance-maker Sunbeam Corp said on Tuesday it was halving its workforce to 6,000 in a cost-cutting program meant to save $225 million a year.

The company also said in a news release it was taking a one-time charge against earnings of $300 million and would slash by 87 percent, or by nearly 10,000, the number of items it manufactures and sells.
The company did not specify when the charge would be taken, and a spokesman was not immediately available.
Only $75 million of the charge will be in cash through the payment of severance and other employee costs, lease obligations and other plant costs, Sunbeam said in the news release.
Under new chief executive Al Dunlap since last summer, Sunbeam said about three quarters of the savings would kick in during 1997 and the remainder the following year.
Savings will come mainly from administrative job cuts, centralizing procurement, and cutting products, Sunbeam said.

Sunbeam will sell or shut 39 of 53 facilities, including 18 of its 26 factories. That will leave Sunbeam, a maker of gas grills, lawn furniture and household goods, with four U.S. factories and four foreign factories.
In addition, total warehouses will be cut to 24 from 61.

Sunbeam will sell several businesses, including furniture, time and temperature, the Counselor and Borg scale lines and a decorative bedding operation. Chase Securities Inc has been hired to sell the units, Sunbeam said.
A purchaser will also be sought for Sunbeam's textile mill in Biddeford, Maine.
Twelve production facilities are expected to be eliminated or sold in connection with the disposition of non-core business lines,reducing headcount by 3,300 jobs.

Sunbeam also said it will eliminate excess production capacity in its core businesses, by closing six additional production facilities and reducing its production workforce by an additional 2,100 persons.

Sunbeam expects to consolidate its current divisional and regional headquarters functions in Chicago, Nashville, Miami, Schaumburg, Ill., Neosho, Mo., and Fort Lauderdale, Fla. into a single worldwide headquarters in Delray Beach, Fla.
As a result, headquarters staff will be reduced from 308 to 123 persons.
Sunbeam said its remaining businesses will be centered on kitchen appliances, personal care products, health care items, outdoor cooking equipment and professional care products.

"Our goal is to essentially complete the restructuring initiatives within the next 45 days. Therefore, the company has every intention of meeting its previously stated goal of beginning 1997 as a new company," Dunlap said.

Sunbeam also said it plans to double revenues to $2 billion by 1999 and lift operating margins to 20 percent of sales from the 2.5 percent posted for the first nine months of 1996. Sunbeam also wants return on equity to grow to 25 percent from one percent in the past year.

International sales will triple to $600 by 1999, Sunbeam said. It said it expects to reach deals with 15 international distributors or licensees over the next five months for such countries as China, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines, Taiwan, Brazil and Australia.
The company also said it will next week start an advertising campaign for some products and move into new sales avenues such as catologs.
-- Michael Connor, New York Newsdesk 212-859-1713
